about: Newcastle and Tyne and Wear leads, 2026-11-03 northern England verify pass.

leads.name: Ancient Pear, Heaton Park
leads.place: Heaton Park, Newcastle, on the main path SW past the Sambuca's Pavilion area, bowling green on the right, interpretation board a few paces on
leads.reason: single blog source, no age or girth, no coordinate found. Needs the park interpretation board text or a council page as second source, plus a pin.

leads.name: Turkey Oak by the Banqueting Hall, Jesmond Dene
leads.place: Jesmond Dene, beside the Banqueting Hall (54.99,-1.59 area)
leads.source: sitelines.newcastle.gov.uk/SMR/5005 (Tyne and Wear HER): planted 1884 at the opening by the Prince and Princess of Wales, 'still survives'
leads.reason: one source (the council HER, an official record), documented planting date for this specimen (1884, so about 140 years); no pin, no girth, not yet shown to be big. Candidate for a later pass: it is a specimen with a documented planter, but a 140-year Turkey Oak may not clear 'worth the walk'.

leads.name: The King (famous oak) at Gibside
leads.source: 1808 archive catalogue entry (National Archives Discovery) mentions a valuation of 'a famous oak tree called The King'
leads.reason: no evidence it still stands; Long Walk avenue itself is an avenue (blocked as a collectible point). Ask NT only via a later pass.

leads.name: Heaton's Shoe Tree
leads.source: Chronicle 2020 and inkl: Tree of the Year shortlist
leads.reason: not researched: species and position unknown this pass, and a shoe tree's draw is a custom, not an old tree.

blocked.name: Town Moor trees
blocked.reason: open common with mostly new planting (12,000 trees planned); no individual veteran identified.
